## About these materials

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Citation statement
Please cite these materials as: Renard, S., Von Grebmer zu Wolfsthurn, S. (2026). *Beyond the lecture: activating learners in academic teaching* [PowerPoint slides]. [LMU PROFIL](https://www.lmu.de/profil/de/). [https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/activation-methods](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/activation-methods)
:::

**Welcome!** In this workshop, **provide future open research instructors and train-the-trainers** explore how **short activation methods** can **support attention, engagement, and learning processes** in higher education teaching and when teaching about open research Especially in longer, input-heavy, or hybrid learning settings, small interactive interventions can help learners stay **focused**, cognitively engaged, and **actively involved**. You will **experience** and **reflect** on a range of low-threshold activation methods that can easily be **integrated into different teaching formats** with **minimal preparation effort**. The workshop combines short theoretical inputs with practical exercises, and reflection activities, enabling you to directly **connect the methods** to your **own teaching practice** in the context of open research


### Who are these materials for?

- **Future open research train-the-trainers** teaching *other* open research instructors or educators in higher education (e.g., universities, colleges) and
- **Aspiring open research instructors** and **self-learners**  

with familiarity about open research challenges, issues and tools.


### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;">
| Prerequisite   |  Description  | Link/Where to find it   |
|------------|------------|------------|
| Familiarity with Open Science concepts and practices | Examples: Replication crisis, open access, R, version control, preregistration, etc.| [Click here to get familiar with Open Research first](https://lmu-osc.github.io/training/self-learning.html) |
| Didactic principles | A firm grasp on didactic tools for teaching | [Click here to get familiar with didactic principles](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/teaching-open-research/core-didactic-principles/) |
| Concept planning | Familiarity with techniques to plan, design and structure an Open Research event | [Click here to get familiar with planning and Open Reserch event principles](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/teaching-open-research/concept-planning/) |
| Creating a positive learning environment | Familiarity with techniques to create a productive and safe learning environment in an open research workshop context | [Click here to get familiar with this topic](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/teaching-open-research/creating-positive-environment/) |
</div>

### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you will be able to...

- **Describe** how instructors can design workshops to support learning
- **Explain** the ICAP framework (Chi, 2009)
- **Reflect on** how different activation methods match a specific learning objective
- **Practice** different activation methods and reflect on their implementation into learners' respective teaching environments
